images.caption: Figure 1:LayerEditor edits images into reusable RGBA layers with user-specified layer content. The predicted layers can be independently manipulated for subsequent edits.

Figure 2:Overview of LayerEditor.
LayerEditor jointly generates the edited canvas𝒟\mathcal{D}and ordered RGBA stack𝒮\mathcal{S}. C-EPD uses the frozen teacher to supervise both the Direct prediction and the decoded composition reconstructed from the predicted layers.

Figure 3:Overview of LayerEditor-100K. Paired editing examples and ordered RGBA annotations cover text, object, and poster-level appearance edits with22–1010layers, providing supervision across diverse editing tasks and layer structures.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison of layered editing. All method outputs are rendered from the predicted RGBA stacks rather than the independently generated canvases. LayerEditor follows the editing instructions while producing coherent recompositions and reusable layers.

Figure 5:Prompt-conditioned layer-content control. Both examples request six RGBA layers with specified layer content. LayerEditor performs the requested edits while assigning text rows and birds to the corresponding reusable layers.
Figure 6:Image-to-layer decomposition on Crello test set.
Figure 7:Effect of C-EPD on recomposed outputs.

Figure 8:LayerEditor-100K construction pipeline.
Two complementary routes create editing pairs with reusable RGBA annotations from native designs and flattened editing pairs. Shared validation checks editing fidelity, layer quality, and reconstruction before export.

Figure 11:Rubric score examples. For the same editing request, progressively improved outputs receive higher scores across editing fidelity, layer separation, composition, and Alpha quality. The examples illustrate the rubric’s discriminative behavior rather than agreement with human ratings.

Figure 12:Instruction-following editing and controllable layer decomposition onCrello-Testset. Prompts specify the edit and layer count. Large output images show recompositions, and checkerboard panels show individual RGBA layers.

Figure 13:Instruction-following editing and content-controlled layer decomposition onScaleEdit-Testset. Prompts specify the edit, layer count, and desired content separation. Large output images show recompositions, and checkerboard panels show individual RGBA layers.
